definition: Bixonimania is a fake disease invented by researchers to examine artificial intelligence and its ability to utilize information in medical and healthcare applications.
details: The fake enabled researchers to show that some AI chatbots would report fake research as fact, while a medical expert would be able to tell that it is fake.

explainer.lead: Bixonimania is a made-up disease used to test whether medical AI chatbots can distinguish fabricated information from facts. Some chatbots repeated fake research about it as true, while a medical expert could spot the invention, highlighting a risk in trusting AI health answers.

tiers.eli5: Imagine making up an illness and a pretend school report about it, then seeing who repeats the report as true. Researchers did this with Bixonimania and AI chatbots: some treated fake research as fact, while a medical expert spotted the trick. It shows why computer answers about health need checking.
tiers.practitioner: Use Bixonimania as a fabricated-medical-information probe when assessing an AI chatbot for medical or healthcare use. Inspect whether its answer repeats fake research as fact rather than accepting fluency or detail as validation; the reported finding applies to some chatbots, not all of them.
tiers.paperLevel: In plain-text notation: probe := fictitious disease + fictitious research; failure := chatbot reports the research as fact. Some AI chatbots exhibited this failure, whereas a medical expert could identify the fabrication. The result does not establish broader clinical validity or show that every chatbot behaves the same way.

explainer.example: Given fabricated research about Bixonimania, a chatbot repeats the claims as factual medical information. A medical expert instead recognizes that the disease is fake.

usedIn.name: Medical AI chatbot evaluation
usedIn.detail: Tests whether a chatbot presents fabricated research as fact.

usedIn.name: Healthcare information applications
usedIn.detail: Probes how AI uses supplied medical information.

explainer.intuition: A fabricated disease provides a clear test: there is no genuine medical knowledge for a chatbot to rely on. If it presents fake research about the disease as fact, the response reveals a failure to recognize the fabrication.
howItWorks: Present the material to AI chatbots.
Check whether chatbots report it as fact.
Compare this with a medical expert identifying the fake.
explainer.whyItMatters: The test exposes how a medical chatbot can turn fabricated research into convincing-sounding factual claims. That makes expert scrutiny important when AI is used for medical or healthcare information.
misconceptions: Bixonimania is not a real disease.
A detailed chatbot answer does not prove that its medical claims are verified.
The finding concerns some chatbots, not every AI system.
